channel.title: Farsçadan (English)
channel.description: AI-assisted English translations of selected stories from Iran's Persian-language press. Every story notes the outlet's political orientation.

item.title: Drone attack in Kuwait kills 2 Italian technicians: Tehran denies responsibility
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Two Italian technicians repairing air defense systems in Kuwait were killed in a drone attack; Tehran denies responsibility while sides blame each other. (Source: Ettelaat)

item.title: Dollar surpasses 295,000 tomans on free market: shopkeepers closing doors
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: In Iran, the dollar surpassed 295,000 tomans on the free market; as inflation climbed to 88.7%, many shopkeepers reported closing their businesses. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: Iran press: claim that gas exports to Turkey extended to 2032 could not be verified
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Iran's press reported BOTAS extended gas imports to 2032; the claim could not be verified by foreign sources. (Source: Ettelaat)

item.title: Methanol poisoning spreads nationwide in Iran: 600 hospitalized, at least 26 dead
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Methanol poisoning from counterfeit liquor spread across Iran, hospitalizing 600; at least 26 died and 9 experienced brain death. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: Truckers' strike in Iran enters day 5: protests spread to 20 cities
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: In Iran, a truckers' strike protesting diesel shortages and rising tire and spare parts prices spread to 20 cities on its fifth day. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: What is the "Axis of Resistance": Iran's regional partners and the network's structure
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: The origins, structure and figures of the "Axis of Resistance" linking Hezbollah, Houthis, militias, and the Quds Force, explained with sources. (Source: Farsçadan)

item.title: Kushner: We've met with Iranian representatives multiple times; all options are on Trump's table
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Kushner said he has met multiple times with Iranian representatives; Trump is focused on Iran and all options remain under consideration. (Source: Donya-ye Eqtesad)

item.title: Pezeshkian: We're talking to the U.S., but we won't yield to bullying
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Pezeshkian said Iran is in talks with the U.S. but will not yield to pressure; in 'no war, no peace' limbo, planning for the future remains difficult. (Source: Donya-ye Eqtesad)

item.title: Baghdad denies claims of troop movements toward Kurdistan Region
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Iraq's government denied reports of troop movements toward the Kurdistan Region after the Federal Court ruling on border authority; tensions remain high. (Source: IRNA)

item.title: Rapidly expanding underground facility alleged between Natanz and Isfahan
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: ISIS satellite imagery shows rapid underground construction between Natanz and Isfahan; the purpose remains unclear according to Iran International. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: Blast near tanker off Dubai: UKMTO reports unidentified object detonation
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: UKMTO reported an unidentified object detonated near a tanker 50 nautical miles west of Dubai; crew reported safe. (Source: IRNA)

item.title: How do Iranian elections work? Candidate vetting, ballots, and turnout figures
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Presidential, parliamentary, and Assembly of Experts elections: candidate vetting, turnout figures, and 2024 results, with sources. (Source: Farsçadan)

item.title: Baghdad centralizes Kurdish oil fields; Erbil rejects move as 'unacceptable'
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Iraqi PM Zeydi linked northern oil fields to federal control after smuggling investigation; KRG's Barzani called the move "entirely unacceptable." (Source: Iran International)

item.title: Saudi jets strike Hodeidah; Sanaa names all Saudi Red Sea ports as targets
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Saudi warplanes hit Yemen's Hodeidah port and international airport; Houthi spokesman warned all Saudi ports on the Red Sea are now targets. (Source: IRNA)

item.title: Iran's press says 'CIA cyberattack'; U.S. says classified systems unaffected
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: CIA and ODNI's open-source intelligence network was breached; U.S. officials said classified systems were not compromised. (Source: Donya-e Eqtesad)

item.title: Truckers in Iran strike for third day; cargo halted in 15 cities
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Protesting dollar-based price hikes on tires and fuel, truckers across 15 Iranian cities stopped hauling cargo for the third consecutive day. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: In Ekbatan case, execution halted at last minute; UN calls for M.A. and N.N.
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Executions of M.A. and N.N. in Ekbatan case halted last minute after families and UN pressure; case enters third year. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: Turkey-Iran relations: trade, natural gas, borders, and regional rivalry
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Turkey and Iran share a 1639 border, pursue $30B annual trade, have a 1996 gas deal ending in 2026, and face migration and smuggling pressure. (Source: Farsçadan)

item.title: Three tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz, burst into flames; stern warning from IRGC Navy
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: IRGC Navy announced three tankers struck naval mines and caught fire in Strait of Hormuz; U.S. air support failed to prevent the incident. (Source: Hamshahri)

item.title: Central Bank chief: Our reserves eroded by $51 billion since Iran war began
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Central Bank chief Karahan announced gross reserves fell from $210 billion to $159 billion since war began—a $51 billion decline. (Source: Hamshahri)
